title: One silent transition on a canonical frame
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and let $q,q'$ be states among the $35$ states. Choose input positions $i,i'\le |x|$, counter length $n$, a second-tape content function $B$, head positions $a,b,a',b'\in\mathbb{Z}$, output word $o$, and signs $m,d_0,d_1\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose the clamped input-head move from position $i$ to position $i'$ is $m$, the counter and second-tape heads move respectively from $a$ to $a'$ and from $b$ to $b'$, and the machine's transition in state $q$ on input symbol $x[i]$ and the symbols under those work-tape heads is silent, writes nothing, and enters state $q'$. Then one step from the canonical frame in state $q$ yields the canonical frame in state $q'$ at position $i'$, with unchanged counter length and tape contents and unchanged output.
hypotheses_covered: specified silent transition on the current input and work-tape symbols
replaced:
If the transducer's transition at the current state, input symbol, and work
symbols is a silent action with no writes, then one machine step from the
canonical reduction frame changes only the control state and the three head
positions, as prescribed; the counter length, buffer, and output are unchanged.
